full_judgment:
18. While the matter is fixed for delivery of judgment the learned Attorney General Mr. Mahbubey Alam, in his private capacity, appeared in the case and upon filing an application under the provision of Order XLI rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure drawn the attention of this Court to the fact that earlier the pre-emptee failed the original copy of DP Parcha, being Khatian No. 1(DP) in the trial Court which shows that there exists a intervening road in between the transferred land and the land owned by the pre-emptor. But as the said Parcha was not marked as exhibit, the learned Courts below failed to consider the same in order to assessing the facts whether there exists any Government road in between the two plots. 

 25. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the impugned judgment and other materials on record including the Advocate Commissioner's report and the DP Parcha being Khatian No. 1(DP). We have also considered the legal aspects of the case in its true perspective. 

 33. In assessing the property of the claim that this Court should examine the requirement of the annexed document in adjudicating the case we have examined all the annexed document I, e; the DP Khatian No. 1 Annexure-B, standing in the name of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, the certificate issued by the Chairman, West Anwara Union Parishad No. 9, dated 25-1-2010, annexure-C, and the letter issued by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Golapgonj, Sylhet, dated 3-1-2010, Annexure-C(1) and found that these documents are of recent origin not in existence at the time of arising of the action of the preemption case and, as such, not at all relevant for the purpose of disposal of the preemption case. Documents which have been subsequently created cannot be taken into consideration for the adjudication of a cause which had arisen earlier specially in a pre-emption proceeding, which has been treated by long standing proposition, as clog in the right to acquire property by the citizens. The Court below since correctly came to the concurrent finding as to the non-existence of any public Road in between the land transferred and the land of the preemptor, this Court finds that there is no requirement to interfere with concurrent finding of facts arrived at by the Courts below. If any concurrent finding is not tainted with perversity or illegally the same cannot be interfered with.
